2608.19902.title: Bringing analytic rigor to agentic AI for science: The Brain Researcher platform for neuroimaging data analysis
2608.19902.paper_summary: AI agents can execute scientific analyses, but an analytic output becomes a defensible claim only after alternatives are weighed and the claim is limited to what the evidence supports. Agents may reproduce failures including selective analysis, premature declarations of success and optimization of imperfect criteria. We present Brain Researcher, an agentic research harness operating in a neuroimaging researcher's computational environment under rules for admissible analyses, required checks and claim scope. In benchmarks, Brain Researcher increased first-choice tool-selection accuracy across seven models by 70.2 percentage points (23.3% without it versus 93.6% with it) and verifiable grounding from 4.6% to 22.0%. In collaborator-led and self-evolving studies, multiverse analyses exposed analytic-choice sensitivity, and scientific review classified claims as accepted, qualified, revised, blocked, rejected or deferred. By linking decisions to evidence and provenance, Brain Researcher embeds methodological judgment within the workflow, not after it.
2608.19902.paper_summary_zh: AI代理可以執行科學分析，但只有在權衡替代方案並將主張限制於證據所支持的範圍內，分析結果才成為可辯護的主張。代理可能會重現失敗，包括選擇性分析、過早宣告成功和對不完善標準的優化。我們介紹了Brain Researcher，一個在神經影像研究者的計算環境中運作的代理研究工具，遵循可接受分析的規則、所需檢查和主張範圍。在基準測試中，Brain Researcher在七個模型中將首選工具選擇的準確性提高了70.2個百分點（沒有它時為23.3%，有它時為93.6%），可驗證的基礎從4.6%提高到22.0%。在合作者主導和自我演變的研究中，多元宇宙分析揭示了分析選擇的敏感性，科學評審將主張分類為接受、合格、修訂、阻止、拒絕或延遲。通過將決策與證據和來源聯繫起來，Brain Researcher將方法論判斷嵌入工作流程中，而不是在之後。
